title: Bound async preview work and define generated Unity-object ownership
description:
## User Mandate

> "Sythesize these into durable tasks. Ensure nothing is lost. We're trying to emphasize consolidation, deduping, decomposition of god classes, and other codebase health improvements"

STRICT. Binding constraints:
- Preserve every accepted mechanism from the 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-03 audits in a durable owner or explicit rejected/unresolved record.
- Consolidate overlapping async preview, stale-result, generated-object lifetime, and editor decomposition work instead of creating parallel task families.
- Preserve deterministic synchronous fallback behavior and authoritative DNA ownership.

## Summary

Harden the asynchronous preview boundary after the first scheduler/controller slice. Bound stale work, remove double definition capture, carry request-scoped diagnostics, and define ownership and domain-reload behavior for generated Unity preview objects.

## Scope

- Make latest-request-wins bound queued work with one running request and at most one queued request, or an equivalent measured policy.
- Choose one owner for detached definition capture. The scheduler and preview controller must not both clone the same request. The current branch intentionally exposes `EnqueueCaptured` for the editor assembly after the preview controller owns the detached capture; do not restore the double-clone path while completing this task.
- Carry sequence, revision, validation summary, failed stage, and failure classification with the generation result.
- Distinguish current, superseded, disposed, cancelled, domain, infrastructure, and unexpected completion states with a minimal contract.
- Make the preview controller the explicit owner of generated Mesh, MeshCollider, GameObject, and child preview objects. Never destroy source assets.
- Define and test domain-reload policy, accepted-result identity, replacement cleanup, and late-result disposal.
- Keep CreatureEditorWindow as coordinator and route complete result application through the preview controller.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Repeated preview requests do not create unbounded queued work, and superseded work is not started when it is already known stale.
- A request captures the definition exactly once and the synchronous Generate path remains a deterministic reference.
- Failure UI displays diagnostics captured for the failed request, never mutable validation state for a newer definition.
- Replacing or disposing a preview releases generated Unity objects without destroying source mesh/material assets.
- Domain reload follows one documented policy and leaves no stale accepted artifact or leaked generated object.
- Focused scheduler and editor tests cover coalescing, disposal, result identity, diagnostic correlation, replacement, and late completion. Unity SceneView smoke validation covers drag, cancellation, stale blocking, collider replacement, and domain reload.

## Validation

Run runtime/editor builds, focused scheduler tests, and the full available Unity EditMode/PlayMode suites. Perform the required Unity SceneView and domain-reload manual checks. Record queue depth, clone count, completion disposition, and generated-object cleanup evidence.

## Findings

Sources S05 and S06, F-12 through F-19 and F-36 through F-38: the scheduler starts every request and only suppresses stale application; PreviewController and scheduler both clone; result failure context is incomplete; generated Unity-object ownership and domain-reload policy are implicit; the controller remains a broad policy hub. TSK-0103 is correctly retained as the completed async foundation, not reopened for its validated parity slice. This follow-up owns the residual boundary work and coordinates with CC-094 and CC-052/061.

## Blockers

Unity execution is required for SceneView lifecycle, domain reload, and Unity-object destruction evidence. Do not mark Done from static inspection alone.

## Next Step

Define the request/result and ownership contracts, then add the smallest scheduler coalescing and preview cleanup tests before implementation.

comments.body:
Audit synthesis 2026-09-12 (CC-AUDIT-GEN-20260912-83C17B4E, CC-AUDIT-20260912-7A5E0C31): canonical owner for bounded async preview work. Verified consolidated scope against current source:

- GP-01 / F-04 (Confirmed, verified): `CreatureGenerationScheduler.EnqueueCaptured` increments `_latestSequence` then calls `Task.Run` immediately for every request (`CreatureGenerationScheduler.cs:48`); `TryTakeCompleted` marks older results stale only after the work is done (`:59`). This is latest-result-wins, not latest-work-wins. A ten-frame slider drag can run ten full generations that only one can present.
- GP-02: `Dispose` sets `_disposed` and advances `_latestSequence` but does not cancel running work (`:64`-`:69`). Late completions can still allocate; safe only while results are pure managed data.
- GP-03: no backpressure metrics (queued, active, canceled, stale-completed, per-stage duration, peak memory).
- GP-06: `Enqueue` clones and `EnqueueCaptured` assumes detached ownership; the difference is documented only in XML comments.
- GP-08 / F-16: `CreatureRuntimePreview` coordinates request, acceptance, mesh assembly, rig build, skin binding, rigid geometry, material fallback and cleanup — lifecycle god-object pressure. Decompose by state ownership, not by line count.
- GP-09 / F-17: higher-level preview replacement is not transactional even though `CreatureRig.Build`, `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer.Bind` and mesh assembly now build-before-swap. Rule: build complete replacement state, perform one ownership commit, dispose superseded state second.

Required architecture (already the correct direction): one active request; at most one replaceable pending request; latest pending overwrites older pending; cooperative cancellation where generation supports it; accepted-result identity check; late-result resource disposal; domain-reload policy; request-scoped diagnostics with a request token carrying cancellation + ownership.

Explicitly rejected by the audit: a superficial fixed-size queue cap, and "cancel every prior Task" as the whole answer (non-cooperative Unity/native work may continue).

Acceptance evidence: burst edits coalesce and stale work does not grow without bound; a failed replacement leaves the prior valid preview intact; domain reload leaves no duplicate components or leaked generated objects.

Provenance caveat: audit bases are not ancestors of current HEAD `b5ba54b`; cited symbols were re-verified in the worktree. Related: TSK-0098, TSK-0219.

Corroborated 2026-09-12 by the metaball pivot synthesis: `docs/audits/creaturecreator-spore-metaball-pivot-and-appearance-synthesis-2026-09-12.md` (report `CC-SYNTH-SPORE-PIVOT-20260912-A7E4D1`), finding F-06.

The synthesis confirms GP-01 from `creaturecreator-audit-generation-performance-lifecycle-2026-09-12.md`: the scheduler starts every request immediately and rejects stale results only after the work completes. A ten-frame drag therefore produces ten costly generations even though nine can never be presented.

No new scope is created here. The level-of-detail task TSK-0225 will consume this scheduler and must not create a competing path. Two requests from TSK-0225 back into this task:
1. Expose the bounded-scheduler counters from GP-03 (queued, active, cancelled, stale-completed) so the interactive tier can prove it coalesces.
2. Confirm whether cancellation is required for the interactive tier or whether one-running plus one-pending is sufficient. TSK-0225 assumes the latter.

No code change made.
